SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 097-2019
  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF CITY OF HAWAIIAN
  GARDENS, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  ESTABLISHING BOUNDARIES AND FORMING THE UNDERGROUND
  UTILITY -DISTRICT NO. 2019-01 ON A SEGMENT OF NORWALK
  BOULEVARD IN THE CITY OF HAWAIIAN GARDENS

SUMMARY

The Community Development Director is requesting that the City Council approve
Resolution No. 097-2019 thereby establishing boundaries and forming the Underground
Utility District (UUD) No. 2019-01 on a portion of Norwalk Boulevard in the City of
Hawaiian Gardens.

DISCUSSION

The Hawaiian Gardens City Council Approved Resolution No. 092-2019 at their regular
scheduled meeting on September 10, 2019. This Resolution set the Public Hearing for
establishing boundaries and forming the Underground Utility District No. 2019-01, in the
City of Hawaiian Gardens for October 8, 2019. All property owners and utility
companies have been sent letters notifying them of the City's intent to form the
Underground Utility District No. 2019-01, and that a Public Hearing on this matter will be
held on October 8, 2019, at the regular City Council meeting.

The City of Hawaiian Gardens has met with Southern California Edison Company to
discuss the possibility of the establishment of Underground Utility District No. 2019-01,
along Norwalk Boulevard from a point 100 feet south of southerly right-of-way line of
Tilbury Street, proceeding north along Norwalk Boulevard to 100 feet north of 215 th
Street northerly right-of-way line, and 100 feet west and east of Norwalk Boulevard
right-of- way limit lines. The estimated date to complete the undergrounding is
December 2021.

Several important reasons exist for establishing Underground Utility District No.
   P.8
2019-01, along Norwalk Avenue. By relocating and undergrounding the utility lines, the
public visibility of this portion of Norwalk Avenue would be substantially improved.

Each Underground Utility District must be established pursuant to City of Hawaiian
Gardens' Ordinance No. 89, which outlines the regulations and the procedures for the
removal of overhead utility facilities. A copy of Ordinance No. 89, is attached for your
review.

In the Fall of 2018, accumulated balance of Rule 20A funds for the City of Hawaiian
Gardens, was $881,822. The annual allocation is $30,728. The yearly funding
allocations are carried over into the fund balance annually. Southern California Edison
has estimated the cost of constructing underground facilities for Underground Utility
District No.2019-01 at $1,100,000. The City would be required to use the option to
mortgage future Rule 20A funds up to next five years to cover the District cost.

The cost of undergrounding power lines would be paid with Rule 20A funds collected by
the Southern California Edison Company. Any other utility company (Cable TV, and
Phone), currently overhead along the Norwalk Boulevard, will bear their own cost.

A Public Hearing is required prior to the for formation of Underground Utility District No.
2019-01.

FISCAL IMPACT

Neither the City of Hawaiian Gardens nor the Property Owners/Tenants will incur cost of
the undergrounding of utilities. The cost of undergrounding for electrical service will be
paid for by the Southern California Edison Rule 20A Funds and other overhead utilities
located within the District.

RECOMMENDATION:

  1. Staff recommends that the City Council conduct the Public Hearing.
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 097-2019.

  WHEREAS, the City Council desires to establish an underground utility district on
 Norwalk Boulevard from 100 ft south of Tilbury Street to 100 ft north of 21 sth Street; and

  WHEREAS, on October 8, 2019, a public hearing was held in the Council
 Chambers in the City Hall, Hawaiian Gardens, California to ascertain whether the public
 necessity, health safety or welfare requires the removal of overhead distribution wires
 and associated overhead structures, and the underground installation of wire and
 facilities for supplying electric, communication, cable television, or similar or associated
 service, except Transmission lines and poles, within the certain area of the City as
 follows:

  That portion of Norwalk Boulevard, in the City of Hawaiian Gardens, County of Los
· Angeles, State of California, as shown in the Undergrounding Utility District No. 2019-01
  Map, bounded as follows:

  Northerly, 100 ft north of northerly Right-of-Way line of 215 1h Street;
  Southerly, 100 ft south of southerly Right-of-Way line of Tilbury Street;
  Westerly, 100 ft west of westerly Right-of-Way line of Norwalk Boulevard;
  Easterly, 100 ft east of easterly Right-of-Way line of Norwalk Boulevard.

  WHEREAS, notice of such hearing was given to all affected property owners as
are shown on the last equalized assessment roll and to all utilities concerned in the
matter within the time required by law; and

  WHEREAS, the hearing has been duly and regularly held and all persons
interested have been given an opportunity to be heard.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
THE CITY OF HAWAIIAN GARDENS AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The recitals are incorporated herein by reference.

  Section 2. That, pursuant to Ordinance No. 89 of the City of Hawaiian Gardens,
the above-described area be established as City of Hawaiian Gardens' Underground
Utility District No. 2019-01. ·

  Section 3. The area proposed to be included in the District is shown upon that
certain map entitled Underground Utility District No. 2019-01, City of Hawaiian Gardens,
which is on file in the office of the City Clerk, City of Hawaiian Gardens and incorporated
herein by reference and attached hereto.
   P. 1 0

  Section 4. That the Council does hereby declare December 31, 2021, as the
date on which affected property owners must be ready to receive underground service,
at the above described property and does hereby order the removal of all poles,
overhead wires and the associated overhead structures and the underground
installation of wires and facilities for supplying electric, communication, or similar or
associated service.

  Section 5. That the City Clerk is hereby instructed to notify all affected utilities
and all persons owning real property within the above described property of the
adoption of this Resolution within ten (10) days of such adoption. Said City Clerk shall
further notify said property owners of the necessity that, if they or any person occupying
such property desire to continue to receive electric, communication or other similar or
associated service, they or such occupant shall, by the date fixed in this resolution,
provide all necessary facility changes on their premises so as to receive such service
from the lines of the supplying utility or utilities at a new location, subject to applicable
rules, regulations, and tariffs of the respective utility or utilities on file with the Public
Utilities Commission of the State of California. Such notification shall be made by
mailing a copy of this resolution together with a copy of said Underground Utility District
No. 2019-01 Map, to all affected property owners as shown on the last equalized
assessment roll and to the affected utilities.

  Section 6. The City Clerk shall notify all affected property owners as shown on
the last equalized assessment roll and utilities concerned of the hearing time and place
by mailing a copy of this resolution at least ten (10) day before the date thereof.

  Section 7. The City Clerk or his/her designee shall attest and shall certify to
the adoption of the Resolution and shall cause this Resolution and his/her certification
to be entered into the Book of Resolutions of the City of Hawaiian Gardens.

PASSED, APPROVED, AND ADOPTED by the City Council of the City of Hawaiian
Gardens on this 8th day of October 2019.

  ADOPT A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER, OR
  DESIGNEE, TO SUBMIT A· GRANT APPLICATION TO THE
  CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT FOR PLANNING GRANTS PROGRAM FUNDING
  UNDER SENATE BILL 2 (SB 2)

SUMMARY

The State of California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
released a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) for grants authorized under the
Planning Grants Program (PGP) provisions of Senate Bill 2 (SB 2). The City of
Hawaiian Gardens may potentially receive a total of $160,000 grant funds from HCD,
with the submittal of a grant application. Staff is requesting City Council's authorization
to proceed and submit a grant application to HCD. Staff is recommending that the
following projects to be included in the SB2 application grant submittal: Reimbursement
of the Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance, Accessory Dwelling Unit Proto-types,
Development of an lnclusionary Housing Ordinance and a Specific Plan for Mix-Use
Development at the Hawaiian Gardens Town Center.

BACKGROUND

The California of Housing and Community Development has implemented a grant
program, known as SB 2, · to provide funding and technical assistance to all local
governments in California to help prepare, adopt, and implement plans and process
improvements that streamline housing approvals and accelerate housing production.

The technical assistance grant provides allocated funding to cities based on population
size. The City of Hawaiian Gardens is eligible to apply for up to $160,000 in funding
and the City is seeking all available funds. The Planning Grant Program will provide
grants through a noncompetitive, over-the-c0unter process to eligible local governments
(cities and counties) who meet the following requirements:

  • Have an HCD-compliant housing element;
   P. 18

  • Have submitted a recent Annual Progress report;
  • Demonstrate a nexus to accelerating housing production; and
  • Demonstrate that the applicant is consistent with State Planning Priorities

DISCUSSION

The City of Hawaiian Gardens is eligible to apply for up to $160,000 in funding and the
City is seeking all available funds. Staff is recommending to City Council to fund the
following city activities:

  1) Reimbursement of Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance
  The City is currently working with a MIG, Incorporated (consultant) on an ADU
  study and has awarded a contracted with MIG, Inc to conduct the analysis, study
  and recommendations to the City based on the State's ADU Law. As part of the
  City's grant application, staff is recommending the reimbursement of the
  consultant's fees. Currently, the consultant will present a draft ADU ordinance to
  the City's Planning Commission on October 9, 2019. If the Planning Commission
  approves the recommendations, the Planning Commissions recommendations to
  the City Council will be presented at a later City Council public hearing for final
  approval of the ADU ordinance.

  2) Accessory Dwelling Unit Prototype
  The City will seek the services of a consultant to study and establish pre-approved
  architectural plans for new Accessory Dwelling Unit at certain locations within the
  City of Hawaiian Gardens. Staff is recommending that the development of these
  new ADU prototypes will be located in neighborhoods where the proposed ADU is
  detached, located at the rear of the lot, and not replacing/removing existing parking
  of the subject site.

  3) lnclusionary Housing Ordinance
  Currently, the City of Hawaiian Gardens does not have rules and guidelines that
  requires developers to sell or rent a certain percentage of new residential units to
  lower-income residents. Staff is recommending in adopting inclusionary housing
  policies with appropriate incentives to accelerate housing development city-wide. ·

  4) Specific Plan for Mix Use Development
  There are several large commercial centers located within the City of Hawaiian
  Gardens that are potentially viable for mix-use development that may integrate mix-
  use development. As part of this analysis, staff recommends to coordinate with a
  consultant to study, analyze and propose a mix-use design of an existing
  commercial center located at the south-west intersection of Norwalk Boulevard and
  Carson Street (Hawaiian Gardens Town Center) that would encourage the
  development of new housing. The study and analysis would allow the consultant to
  review the existing site, propose architectural plans that incorporate housing and
  provide conceptuals for City Council to review. The consultant will be required to

  2
   P. 19

  put together architectural plans that propose a mix-use development that is "shelf-
  ready" with approved land use entitlements.

Staff believes that these four projects will help the City achieve incentives and new
opportunities for housing within the City of Hawaiian Gardens. These four projects are
aimed to capitalize on changes in land use and other investments to make the area
more livable, resilient, and healthy by providing opportunity for needed housing and
enhancing the City's quality of life.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

This resolution is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (Public
Resources Code,§ 2100, et seq; "CEQA"). The adoption of the proposed ordinance is
not a "project" under CEQA and the State CEQA Guidelines (14 Cal. Code of
Regulations, § 15000, et seq.) as it does not have the "potential for resulting in either a
direct physical change in the environment, or a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical
change in the environment." (CEQA Guidelines, §§ 15060 (c) (2)(3), 15378(a).)
Moreover, even if the resolution qualified as a project under CEQA, the Ordinance is
exempt from CEQA as "it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the
activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment." (State CEQA
Guidelines, § 15061 (b)(3).)

FISCAL IMPACT

If awarded the full amount requested, $160,000, the City will have potential funds to
implement the costs associated with the Reimbursement of Accessory Dwelling Unit
Ordinance, create an Accessory Dwelling Unit prototype, create an lnclusionary
Housing Ordinance and Specific Plan for Mix-Use Development for the Hawaiian
Gardens Town Center.

  EVENT EQUIPMENT

BACKGROUND

The Special Events Committee meets throughout the year for planning and logistics
purposes. During the September 2019 meeting discussion were held related to the
holiday event/tree lighting ceremony. At the meeting the Committee approved and
recommended to revert to the use of an artificial tree rather than the live tree used
in 2018. Placement would be at the original location on the median island between
City Hall and the C. Robert Lee A<::livity Center and there would be no need for to
shut-down Pioneer Boulevard or related expenses.

DISCUSSION

The artificial tree used in the past has aged and the committee recommended the
procurement of a replacement. Public Works was tasked with negotiationg with our
holiday vendor, Dekra-lite lo procure a 20' artificial tree. The tree lease with Dekra-
lite will replace and supersede the current agreement for decoration of the live tree
used last year. Dekra-lite worked with City staff to come to terms with a new
agreement with no forfeits and applied the deposits already processed by the City
to the new proposed lease. The new artificial tree will display a predetermined light
show with song/light sequences that repeat every 30 minutes.

  •  Sequoia Tree with Frame, Branches, Topper and Assembly
  •  Hardware

  installed
  •  Spacer cables and smart T's to connect the NOB boxes to the
  branches
  •  Network Switch and switch Box
  •  Category 5 Data Cables to connect the NOB boxes to the controller
  •  Mini Controller with Power Transformer for branch testing
  •  Harbinger 200w speaker with cable to connect sound
  •  Pre-programmed Show on SD Card and installed in NEC
  •  Spare Parts package including: extra cables, NOB Box, and tree
  branches

  In addition to the tree, a cement slab will be poured to ensure a flat/solid foundation
  for current and future decor and platform installation along with an update to
  electrical at the site.

  Cost will total $19,000 for FY19/20 consisting of $14,000 for the tree and site
  preparation costs related to installation of cement slab in the median island for the
  tree platform and associated electrical work estimated at $5,000.

  RECOMMENDATION

  It is recommended that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter into
  terms with Dekra-Lite to amend live tree lease and substitute with artificial tree
  lease.

SUMMARY

Staff received direction from Mayor Maravilla to introduce a new residential Block
Wall Program. The intent of the Program is to build a block wall to evenly divide
property lines, which were extended to properties that at one point had an alley
between them before they were vacated in the 1970s.

DISCUSSION

The Block Wall Program may provide assistance to the following residential
properties: single family properties and duplex properties.

Preference will be given to those properties that are adjacent to a vacated alley.
During the 1970s, certain alleyways in the City were vacated. However, as a result of
those vacations, the existing fences and/or walls on certain properties abutting these
vacated alleyways were no longer entirely aligned with the property line. In other
words, the vacation of these alleyways created the resulting need for relocating
and/or replacing walls. Although some walls have been relocated and/or replaced
over time, many have not; given the length of time since the alleyway vacations,
many properties are in need of addressing these walls.

In the event that there are remaining available funds for the Block Wall Program after
all applications for properties adjacent to a vacated alley (and that otherwise meet all
the requirements of the Block Wall Program Guidelines) have been provided grants,

I. PROGRAM OVERVIEW AND PURPOSE

The intent of the Block Wall Program ("Program") is to assist residents with building a
block wall to divide property lines, some of which were extended to properties that at one
point had an alley between them before they were. vacated in the 1970s. The City of
Hawaiian Gardens shall provide assistance through the Block Wall Program to eligible
applicants ("Applicant") residing within City limits.

Funding for the Program comes from the City's General Fund. The Program is available
to any City of Hawaiian Gardens residents who qualify based upon a satisfactory
application, neighbor agreements (enclosed in the application), and funding availability.
This is a voluntary program that requires all parties affected by the construction of the
block wall to be in agreement of its location before construction may begin.

The City of Hawaiian Gardens may provide Program assistance to the following
residential properties:

  ✓ Single Family Properties
  ✓ Duplex Properties

Preference will be given to those properties that are adjacent to a vacated alley,

The primary purpose of the Program is to address the need-originally created as a result
of certain alleyways being vacated during the 1970s-for relocating and/or replacing
walls. Although some of the affected walls have been relocated and/or replaced over time,
many have not, and given the length of time since the alleyway vacations, are in need of
assistance to address this issue. In the event that there are available funds remaining for
the Program after all applications for properties adjacent to a vacated alleyway (and that
otherwise meet all the requirements of these Guidelines) have been provided grants, the
City may use remaining Program funds for other qualifying properties (i.e., non-adjacent
to vacated alleyways) for purposes of health and safety, beautification, and elimination of
blight

II. PROGRAM SERVICES

The City of Hawaiian Gardens Block Wall Program provides financial assistance, on a
priority basis, to residents who wish to build a block wall to evenly distribute the land

and to block walls adjacent to the sidewalk; any remaining Program funds may be used
for other qualifying properties not adjacent to alleyways for purposes of health and safety,
beautification, and elimination of blight. Program assistance will be available for
residential single family properties or duplex properties.

The Applicant may qualify to receive a block wall built on their property depending on the
configuration of their home and lot lines. Access to the property and an inspection of the
lot will be required to determine the location and size of the block wall.

  The City of Hawaiian Gardens Block Wall Program will offer a grant of up to
  $10,000 to eligible Applicants. The grant may cover demolition of any existing
  fencing that may be in the way of the newly proposed wall, construction of a new
  block wall, and any planning, land surveying or permit fees that may be required
  before construction. All block walls must be approved by the Planning Division of
  the Community Development Department. Applicants will riot be required to pay
  back the grant financial assistance received, but will be subject to the following

  1. The City will contribute, per Applicant, fifty-percent (50%) of the total
  construction cost(s) and the remaining fifty-percent (50%) will be paid by

  2. The City must receive Applicant's share (i.e., fifty-percent (50%)) of the
  construction cost prior to commencing any work; the total cost must be

  4. Program Staff will determine the amount of funding or scope of work for

  RECOMMENDATION

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached City of Hawaiian Gardens Policy
  regarding the Public Records Act (PRA).

  BACKGROUND AND DISCUSSION

  Like all California cities, the City of Hawaiian Gardens is required under the California Public
  Records Act (Gov. Code §§ 6250-6276.48) to make available for inspection and copying
  any City records that are not otherwise exempt from disclosure under State or federal law.
  Normally, the City Clerk's Office handles Public Records Act requests received by the City.
  However, from time to time, various City departments and staff receive requests for copies
  of City records, and this at times may create confusion or inconsistencies for City staff
  members and consultants who may be unfamiliar with the Public Records Act. The Public
  Records Act sets forth specific time frames that apply to responding to such requests,
  consistency in handling all Public Records Act requests is important.

  Accordingly, to create effectiveness, efficiencies and transparency in the handling of Public
  Records Act requests, and to provide guidance to both City employees, consultants, and
  the public regarding such requests and the processes thereof, the attached Public Records
  Act policy has been prepared to establish procedures for handling, processing, and
  responding to requests for inspection and/or copying of official City records. The policy is
  authorized under the Public Records Act, which specifically allows public agencies to adopt
  regulations or guidelines stating the procedures to be followed when making public records
  available. (Gov. Code§ 6253.4)

  Procedure Policy Regarding the Public Records Act

 I.  PURPOSE

  A.  This policy sets forth the City of Hawaiian Gardens' procedures for handling
  requests for inspection and/or copying of public records. It is designed to both
  (i) be in compliance with the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code, §
  6250 et seq., and sometimes referred to herein as the "PRA") and all existing
  laws and regulations pertaining to disclosure of public record, and (ii) create
  efficiencies and transparency in the processing of any such requests. If any
  provision of this policy conflicts with current state or federal law, the law shall
  take precedence.

  B.  This policy is authorized under Government Code section 6253.4, subdivision
  (a), which provides: "Every agency may adopt regulations stating the
  procedures to be followed when making its records available in accordance
  with this section." The PRA and the California Constitution (Art. I, § 3, subd.
  (b)) give every member of the public the right to inspect and/or receive copies
  of public records, for the direct cost of duplication or a statutory fee, except
  where access is otherwise made exempt by law.

II.  DEFINITIONS

  A.  "Public records" or "records" shall include any writing containing information
  relating to the conduct of the public's business that is prepared, owned, used
  or retained by the City, regardless of physical form or characteristics.

  B.  "Writing"  means  handwriting,  typewriting,  printing,  photostatting,
  photographing, photocopying, transmitting by electronic mail or facsimile, and
  every other means of recording upon any tangible thing any form of
  communication or representation, including letters, words, pictures, sounds,
  or symbols, or combination thereof, and any record thereby created,
  regardless of the manner in which the record has been stored ..

Ill.  SCOPE

  The City Clerk shall manage the City's PRA requests. However, to the extent any
  City staff receives a PRA request, they are tasked with prioritizing such requests as
  reasonably permitted by their job duties and notifying the City Clerk's office of such
  requests.

IV.  PROCEDURES

  A.  The PRA Request

  1.  Any member of the public may make a records request. The City
  encourages, but does not require, the requester's name or purpose of
  the request. Anonymous requests or fictitious names are permitted.

   P.92
  2.  The City encourages, but does not require, members of the public to
  submit written PRA requests to the City Clerk's office by electronic
  mail, postal mail, in-person delivery, or a form provided on the City's
  website. If a person submits a request verbally or to a staffer other
  than the City Clerk, then the staffer may recommend that the request
  be put in writing or submitted to the City Clerk's office. However, if the
  requester refuses to do so, then the staffer shall document the request
  and transmit it to the City Clerk's office.

  3.  Once the City receives a PRA request, the City shall stamp the request
  with the date received. The date received is the date that the City first
  learns of the request (i.e., the date of the City business day the
  electronic mail or postal mail is opened). If possible, the City shall also
  mark the request with a reference number for processing purposes.

  4.  All requests received by the City shall be forwarded to the City Clerk's
  office. The City Clerk shall forward any requests involving the City
  Council to the City Attorney and the City Manager.

  5.  If the request does not reasonably identify a City record, then the City
  Clerk shall make every effort to assist the .requester in making a
  focused and effective request. (Gov. Code, § 6253.1, subd. (a).) The
  City Clerk shall document their efforts to assist the requester as
  follows:

  a.  Assist the member of the public to identify records and
  information that are responsive to the request or to the purpose
  of the request, if stated.

  b.  Describe the information technology and physical location in
  which the records exist.

  c.  Provide suggestions for overcoming any practical basis for
  denying access to the records or information sought.

  6.  If the request is modified per Section IV.A.5, above, then the
  modification should be documented in the response letters to the
  requester per Section IV.C, below.

  B.  Gathering Records

  1.  Upon receipt of a request, the City Clerk shall notify and coordinate
  with City staff likely to maintain records responsive to the request. The
  City Clerk and City staff shall gather and review responsive documents
  as expeditiously as possible. This includes responsive records on
  personal devices pursuant to the City of San Jose v. Superior Court
  (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608.

65320.00001\32340747.3
   P,93
  2.  With respect to requests for electronic communications (e.g., electronic
  mail and text messages), it is the City's policy that electronic
  communications that are intended to be retained in the ordinary course
  of the City's business are recognized as official records in need of
  protection/retention in accordance with the California Public Records
  Act, but that all other electronic communications are considered
  "transitory" documents (work-in-progress) and therefore are not usually
  subject to the City's record retention requirements. Because the City's
  electronic communications systems are not designed for long-term
  storage, electronic communications which are intended to be retained
  as an official record will be filed and retained consistent with this policy.

  3.  When gathering records responsive to the request for review, the City
  shall consider whether a reasonable person would conclude that the
  record is responsive, no matter if a legal exception may allow the City
  to withhold the record from production to the public.

  4.  Records gathered as responsive records shall be maintained without
  redaction for at least two years after the date of final production.

  5.  When gathering records, the City shall not create a new record that
  does not otherwise exist, unless the City Clerk expressly authorized
  the new record's creation. The City Clerk shall consult with the City
  Attorney in these instances.

  C.  Responding to the PRA Request

  1.  The City shall initially respond to PRA requests promptly, but no later
  than ten (10) days after the request was received. (Gov. Code, § 6253,
  subd. (c).) For example, if a request is received on February 1, then
  the first day is February 2 and the tenth day is February 11. However,
  if tenth day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or other day in which the City
  is not open to conduct regular City business, then the response is due
  the next business day after the tenth day.

  2.  The City is not required to produce documents within ten (10) days
  after the request, but the City Clerk must respond within ten (10) days
  with one of the following:

  a.  Inform the requester the City has identified responsive records
  and is producing the non-exempt responsive records per
  Section IV.D, below, as part of this response.

  b.  Inform the requester that the City has identified responsive
  records, is reviewing the records, and intends to produce the
  records by a reasonable future date. The response will also
  indicate whether the City intends to produce the documents at
  one time or on a rolling basis. If the City intends to produce
  documents on a rolling basis, then the City should establish a
  tentative schedule with the requester. Guidelines for production
  are as follows:

  (1)  The City should aim to produce a responsive record
  within ten (10) days of the City's response.

  (2)  If the City intends to produce records on a rolling basis,
  and if possible, then the City should aim to produce
  records in no greater than three (3)-week increments.

  c.  Inform the requester that the City has no responsive documents.

  d.  Inform the requester that the City is taking its fourteen (14)-day
  extension afforded by the PRA to determine whether the City
  has any responsive records. (Gov. Code, § 6253, subds. (c)(1)-
  (4).) The City does not need the requester's permission to use
  this extension. After the fourteenth day, the City must respond
  to the requester as provided in subsections a (produce the
  records), b (establish future date of production), or c (no
  responsive records) of this Section IV.C.2, above. The response
  must cite one or more of the following reasons for the extension:

  (1)  The City needs to search for and collect the requested
  records from field facilities or other establishments that
  are separate from the office processing the request.

  (2)  The City needs to search for, collect, and appropriately
  examine a voluminous amount of separate and distinct
  records that are demanded in a single request.

  (3)  The City needs for consultation, which shall be
  conducted with all practicable speed, with another
  agency having substantial interest in the determination of
  the request or among two or more components of the
  agency having substantial subject matter interest therein.

  (4)  The City needs to compile data, to write programming
  language or a computer program, or to construct a
  computer report to extract data.

  D.  Producing the Records

  1.  Format of Production

  a.  City staff may produce responsive non-exempt records digitally
  via electronic mail or on line file sharing.

  b.  City staff may produce responsive non-exempt records via
  delivery of hard copies, a flash drive, CD, or other storage
  device.

  2.  Fees Charged to the Requester

  a.  If a fee is required for production, the City shall produce the
  records promptly after the fee is paid.
65320,00001\32340747.3
   P.95
  b.  The City may not charge the requester a fee to cover the time or
  resources the City expends to gather, process, and review the
  records. Accordingly, if records are produced in the format
  provided in Section IV.D.1.a, above, then the City generally may
  not charge a fee for production.

  c.  The City may charge the requester a fee to cover the direct
  costs to duplicate records. Accordingly, if records are produced
  in the format provided in Section IV.D.1.b, above, then the City
  generally may charge the requester the appropriate fee.

  d.  However, in certain cases, whether production is the format
  provided in Section IV.D.1.a or 1.b, the City may charge the
  requester a fee to cover costs for the City to construct a record
  and the costs of programing and computer services when either
  of the two below instances apply. The City Clerk shall consult
  with the City Attorney in such instances.

  (1)  The City is required to produce a copy of an electronic
  record and the record is one that is produced only at
  otherwise regularly-scheduled intervals.

  (2)  The request requires data compilation, extraction, or
  programming to produce the record.

  E.  Record Review and Exemptions

  1.  The City shall only redact the specific portion of the record that is
  exempt. Redactions should not only black out the information but also
  delete any embedded hyperlinks. Information contained in a record
  that is non-responsive to the PRA request shall not be redacted.

  2.  Responsive records shall be reviewed to assess the following:

  a.  Whether the responsive record is a public record. Non-public
  records may be records that are primarily personal, containing
  no more than incidental mentions of agency business.

  b.  Whether a particular exemption to production applies.

  3.  The list below is of common exemptions provided by the PRA. This list
  is not exhaustive and the City Attorney should be consulted if there is
  any question whether an exemption below or any other exemption
  applies.

  a.  Information or documents may be withheld if the public interest
  in non-disclosure clearly outweighs the public interest in
  disclosure.  (Gov. Code, § 6255.) If the City applies this
  exemption, the response letter must list the name and title of the
  person responsible for claim of exemption.

  b.  Personnel, medical records. (Gov. Code, § 6254, subd. (c).)

BACKGROUND

On January 3, 2019, the City Manager entered into an agreement for limited special
legal services with Megan Garibaldi under the City Manager's contracting authority. On
January 8, 2019, the City Council appointed Megan Garibaldi as Interim City Attorney
and on February 26, 2019, the City Council approved a long-term agreement for Interim
City Attorney services for the City of Hawaiian Garden. It is recommended that the City
Council approve the attached Agreement for Legal Services which will remove the
"Interim" status of Megan Garibaldi, Interim City Attorney and provide the City with
continuing city attorney services.

DISCUSSION

In accordance with Government Code section 36505, the City Council may appoint the
City Attorney. The City Attorney serves as the chief legal advisor to the Council, the
Manager, and all City departments and appointed bodies, and has the authority to
represent the City in all civil and criminal matters, and performs such other duties as
prescribed by the City's Municipal Code, by ordinance or resolution, or as requested by
the Council or City Manager. The City Attorney mush be an attorney at law and duly
licensed to practice in the State of California.

The attached Legal Services Agreement is recommended to continue the services of
Megan Garibaldi and Best Best & Krieger, LLP (BBK) as City Attorney. The attached
agreement continues the provisions of the Interim City Attorney agreement with
exceptions being that it removes the "Interim" designation for City Attorney, provides for
   P.98

a shifting of rates, and a reduction of reimbursable fees. The fees in Exhibit A Scope of
Services and Applicable Billing Rates reflect tiered rates for general legal services,
special legal services, and reimbursed services. Fees for general legal services go
from $215 per billable hour to $245 for City Attorney, remain the same as the prior
agreement at $215 for all other attorneys, and reduce to $180 for certain specified legal
services, as well $160 per billable hour for paralegals. Tiered rate structuring is offered
in an effort to lower billable amounts by providing different rates for lower and more
complex legal matters. Special Legal Services rates remain the same at $315 for
litigation but now also include a rate of $180 in included for Public Information Act legal
services. Additionally, a 10% reduction on reimbursable fees has been incorporated.

This Agreement shall. commence on the Effective Date and remain in effect until
terminated. The City may terminate this Agreement, with or without cause, upon written
notice to BBK. BBK may terminate, with or without cause, on sixty days written notice to
the City. In either event, the City agrees to secure new counsel as quickly as possible
and to cooperate fully in the substitution of the new counsel as counsel of record. BBK
agrees to cooperate fully in any such transition, including the transfer of files.
Notwithstanding the termination of BBK's services, City will remain obligated to pay to
BBK all fees and costs properly incurred prior to termination.

FISCAL IMPACT

The Adopted 101-2019 Citywide Budget includes funds for City Attorney services.
Related fees fluctuate per the City's needs and/or pending litigation.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council discuss and adopt Resolution No. 101-2019
approving an agreement for legal services for the City of Hawaiian Gardens and Best
Best & Krieger.

SUBJECT:  DISCUSSION, REVIEW, AND DIRECTION OF RECREATIONAL FIELD
  USAGE AND.SCHEDULING

SUMMARY

Mayor Maravilla requested that the City Council for discuss, review, and direct staff as
appropriate on the utilization and scheduling of procedures for scheduling of fields under
the City's control.

DISCUSSION

The City of Hawaiian Gardens prides itself in providing numerous sports for youth and
adults. In an effort to accommodate these teams, the Athletic Field Use Rules and
Regulations were created. This document lists the procedures involved in requesting
fields. Consideration for field requests are given in the following order:

  •  City sponsored programs/events;
  •  ABC Unified School District schools/programs;
  •  Local non-profit organizations (chartered by the State of California and 50%
  minimum residency of Participants);
  •  Private Groups/Individuals.

Being that the city lacks open space, we have partnered with the ABC Unified School
district to utilize their local school grounds for athletic purposes. Our collaboration has
enabled the city to provide athletic events at approximately five schools, two of which
have lights for evening use. While the city offers year-round adult/youth sports (football,
volleyball, basketball, soccer, track, baseball, softball) staff also works to schedule our
local youth non-profits with field time.
